decided: A record of apply or archive states where consent came from as one of three values: the user typed the command, the user answered a prompt, or a setting granted it. orbit refuses to write a record claiming a setting granted the command when the chain map does not grant it, and refuses any value outside the three. The first two values are still taken on the session's word.
alternatives: take the third value on the session's word, like the other two
add a separate field naming which key granted the command
why: Whether a setting grants a command is written in a file orbit can read, so the claim can be checked; whether the user typed a command or answered a prompt is not in any file. Each key grants one command, so the value alone says which key it was.

defines.definition: the user's agreement that orbit may start apply or archive; today it comes from the user typing the command or answering a prompt

detail: Values user-invoked, prompted, setting on the consent field of the apply and archive emits; the check reads resolveChainSetting. Named limit: a grant withdrawn between a command's entry and its emit refuses a true record. All 139 apply and archive emits on record carry user-invoked or no field. The AI's method call.
